title: Lutnick Faces Bipartisan Fury Over Alleged AI Chip Leaks to China
snippet: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is drawing intense scrutiny from Capitol Hill following revelations that advanced Nvidia AI chips reached Chinese-linked entities despite strict export controls.
content:
WASHINGTON — Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is finding himself in an increasingly precarious political position as lawmakers from both sides of the aisle vow to crack down on national security lapses that allowed cutting-edge American artificial intelligence chips to flow into China.

The bipartisan backlash follows revelations that semiconductor giant Nvidia sold billions of dollars worth of advanced microchips to Megaspeed, a Singapore-based firm whose former senior executive, Alice Huang, has been accused by U.S. intelligence of having ties to a Chinese spy agency. The scandal has intensified scrutiny over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who admitted to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, as well as President Trump’s intervention to keep Jensen Huang at the helm of the company.

Tensions Explode Within the Cabinet

While members of Congress have limited leverage over Nvidia’s corporate governance, they hold direct oversight over the Department of Commerce — and lawmakers are targeting Lutnick’s handling of export enforcement.

Reports indicate that Lutnick resisted calls from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Secretary of State Marco Rubio to place Megaspeed on a federal trade blacklist. Bessent publicly expressed frustration over the Commerce Department's delay in blocking high-end chip sales, telling reporters that President Trump had made it explicit that China should not receive Nvidia processors superior to the H100 model.

Sens. Mark Warner (D-Va.) and Tom Cotton (R-Ark.), prominent figures on the Senate Intelligence Committee, warned that the Commerce Department may have turned a blind eye to additional shell companies operating across Southeast Asia that funnel high-powered computing resources to Beijing. Cotton emphasized that Congress will press forward with legislation, including his Chip Security Act, to close regulatory loopholes.

Ethical Questions and Calls for Resignation

Lutnick’s troubles extend beyond enforcement delays. Congressional Democrats are raising questions about potential financial conflicts of interest, investigating whether Cantor Fitzgerald — the financial services firm Lutnick previously led and now managed by his sons — maintains financial ties to data centers in Malaysia and Singapore implicated in bypassing U.S. chip restrictions.

Additionally, the Commerce chief is facing heat over a fresh report alleging he reassigned federal agents tasked with investigating illicit chip smuggling to serve on his personal security detail, diverting resources from a critical national security mission.

The mounting controversy has prompted key Republicans to join Democrats in demanding accountability. Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) suggested the Commerce Department appeared to knowingly allow sensitive technology to skirt restrictions, calling for officials to testify under oath. Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) went further, arguing that Lutnick should have intervened when Jensen Huang was invited onto Air Force One despite intelligence briefings regarding the executive's personal entanglements.

“I think he should roll,” Tillis said, calling for Lutnick’s resignation as Senate panels prepare to haul officials in for testimony next month.
